answer: To resist Sybil attacks, each agent identity is bound to a physical telemetry probe anchored at unique coordinates, such as an environmental sensor on a coastal jetty. Every epoch, nodes broadcast signed readings of local thermal plume fluctuations verified against spatial neighbor trees. An attacker cannot virtualize identities across one machine; each fake node requires dedicated tamper-resistant hardware costing $600 plus physical site placement, guaranteeing that identity spoofing burns vastly more capital than any jade protocol rewards.
